KUMAR AGARWALLA: Will the

INDUSTRY be pleased to state:

and European Union have rejected large

SC's observations on the
Representation of the People Act
*202. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE:
SHRI N. K.  PREMACHANDRAN:
Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some time
back the Supreme Court of India has
declared Section 33-B of the Representation
of the People Act as unconstitutional;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have submitted/
decided to submit a review petition in the
matter to the court;

companies
†*203. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the foreign
companies implementing their construction
projects in the country are to employ local
experts and skilled workers;
(b) whether foreign experts and skilled
workmen are brought from abroad as per
the conditions laid down by the World Trade
Organisation whereas there is no dearth of
experts and skilled workmen in the country;
and
(c) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor?

Pilferage of medicines
†*204. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that medicines
supplied for different hospitals were seized
during a raid conducted on the 9th June,
2003 by the Drugs Control Department,
Delhi and the Bureau of Economic
Offences;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of employees of hospitals
and chemists involved in this racket and the
hospitals to which they belong to;
(d) the action taken by Government
against the culprits; and
(e) the arrangements made by
Government to check recurrence of such
incidents in future?
Health for all by 2000
*205. SHRIMATI  SHABANA AZMI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government had a plan for
Health for All by 2000;
(b) the extent to which Government have
implemented the plan so far;
(c) whether it is a fact that despite the
plan 1000 Indians die every day of
tuberculosis and other diseases; if so, the
reasons therefor;
(d) the amount provided to the States in
achieving this plan and the steps taken to
implement this plan so far;
(e) whether there is continuous shortage
of doctors and nurses in the country; and
(f) if so, the extent of shortage of doctors
at present and the steps Government propose
to take to improve the position?
Broadcasting Policy
*206. DR. A.R. KIDWAI:
SHRI AIMADUDDIN AHMAD
KHAN (DURRU):
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to formulate a comprehensive Broadcasting
Policy in view of the massive expansion of
satellite television and private FM radio;
(b) whether a meeting was convened by
his Ministry recently with the broadcasters
to know their views;
(c) if so, whether the draft policy
prepared by his Ministry was also discussed;
(d) if so, the views expressed by the
broadcasters; and
(e) by when the Broadcasting Policy is
likely to be announced?
Conversion of residential property
*207. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
DR. AKHILESH DAS:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to restart the scheme for converting the
residential property from leasehold to
freehold in the capital;
(b) if so, the details of the scheme
especially with respect to sub-leasees of
DDA plots and flats, held through the
cooperative housing societies; and
(c) the number of applications received
and those disposed so far?

Ban on advertisements of liquor and
tobacco products on TV
*208. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a ban
on advertisements of liquor and tobacco
products on TV channels;
(b) whether it is also a fact that some
manufacturers of liquor are advertising their
brands showing their subsidiary products
of the same name; and
(c) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to stop advertising liquor brands to
discourage consumption of liquor and
tobacco?
FDI inflow
*209. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
DR. M.N. DAS:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have adopted
global norms for compiling FDI inflows; if
so, the details in this regard;
(b) whether Government are considering
any proposal to bring FDI data reporting
system into alignment with international best
practices;
(c) if so, what was the FDI inflow target
set for the years 2000-01, 2001-02 and
2002-03;
(d) whether it is a fact that US Companies
are losing interest in investment in the
country and India's aggregate FDI inflow
has shrunk substantially;
(e) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(f) the efforts being made to improve the
FDI approvals in regard to US?
Capitation fee in Medical Colleges
*210. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
 Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that certain Medical
Colleges in Maharashtra, Karnataka and
Tamil Nadu have been charging very high
capitation fee from the students seeking
admission;
(b) if so, whether Government have
made any enquiry to ascertain the factual
position in this regard; and
(c) the action Government have taken
against the management of such Medical
Colleges for violation of Supreme Court
judgement in this regard?
Meat export
†*211. SHRI ISAM SINGH: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the quantity of meat exported every
year; and
(b) the amount of foreign currency being
earned as a result thereof?
Chickenpox cases in Delhi
*212. SHRI RAJU PARMAR: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether cases of chickenpox are on the
rise and are being reported daily at Infectious
Diseases Hospital (IDH) in NCT of Delhi;
(b) if so, the number of cases of
chickenpox reported at IDH during the last
one year, month-wise; and
(c) the steps Government propose to take
to prevent the spread of this dreaded disease
in Delhi?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

WS-3/C:/SESSION/1977RS 64
Expansion of automobile industry
†*213.  SHRI LAJPAT RAI:
SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH
'LALAN':
Will the Minister of HEAVY
INDUSTRIES AND PUBLIC
ENTERPRISES be pleased to state:
(a) the assessment Government have
made regarding the pace of development
and expansion of the industry related to
manufacture of automobiles in the country
during the last five years; and
(b) the production of cars in the country
during the years 2000-01, 2001-02 and
2002-03, separately, and the details of the
export made during each year of the said
period?
Monkey disease
*214. SHRI H.K. JAVARE GOWDA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that during  the
summer scourge of Malnad region in
Karnataka, the Kyasanur Forest Disease
(KFD) or Monkey disease has claimed 10
lives and left 253 people ill;
(b) if so, the number of the affected people
during the past three years;
(c) the steps taken by Government for
prevention of this disease and amount spent
so far during the past five years; and
(d) whether any special grant is
proposed to be provided for eradication of
this disease and if so, the details thereof?
Primary Health Centres in Assam
*215. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of funds allotted to Assam
for setting up of Primary Health Centres
during the last three years, year-wise;
(b) the number of health Centres opened
so far and the expenditure incurred thereon,
year-wise; and
(c) the funds proposed to be given in the
current financial year?
New scheme for population control
†*216. SHRIMATI SAVITA
SHARDA: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
introduce any new schemes to control
population growth keeping in view that the
country has registered an increase in
population of around Eighteen crores during
the last one decade;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the funds Government propose to
allocate for the purpose?
Guidelines for shooting of foreign
feature films
*217. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
SHRI B. J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have liberalised
the guidelines for shooting foreign feature
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

films and co-productions in the country as
part of its endeavour to turn India into an
entertainment hub;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether these liberalised guidelines
have been accepted by the foreign film
producers;
(d) if so, to what extent they have
welcomed this move; and
(e) by when they are likely to be given
permission to shoot foreign films in the
country?
AIDS vaccine
*218. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Scientists at
the National AIDS Research Centre have
recently begun test trials of India's first
AIDS  vaccine—modified vaccinia
Ankara—to counter the strains of HIV sub-
type 'C';
(b) by when the trials on human beings
are expected to take place;
(c) whether the trials that have been
conducted on animals were successful; and
(d) whether permission from the Drug
Controller General of India has been
obtained to get set for phase one of the
human trials?
Reimbursement of medical claims
*219.SHRI R. S. GAVAI:
SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number
of medical reimbursement claims of the
Government employees and pensioners
under the CGHS pertaining to the last
financial year are pending;
(b) the number of claims and the amount
unpaid, State-wise;
(c) by when these claims would be
settled;
(d) the minimum time taken by
Government to settle the claims;
(e) whether Government propose to
modify or hasten the process of
reimbursement; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Mysterious illness affecting children
*220. SHRI EKANATH K.
THAKUR:
SHRI R. P. GOENKA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that experts are
clueless on the mysterious illness that has
killed 87 children in Andhra Pradesh;
(b) if so, the efforts made by Government
to investigate the cause of the illness;
(c) the details of other States affected by
this disease; and
(d) the assistance provided to affected
States?
